text:
This contest aims to encourage the creation of fun and innovative in-hand games (games that do not require a surface, pockets, or anything but your hands to play). With this contest, we hope to encourage all you clever designers to create interesting new gaming experiences.

This is the THIRD edition of the original in-hand game design contest on BGG. It was inspired by the many in-hand games entered into the 2021 Solitaire PnP contest.
We are a team of 2 enthusiastic geeks who have joined forces to bring this contest to life. I, CyBadger, have taken the responsibility of being the general host of this contest, same as last year. Igor Zuber will be in charge of the voting process and helping out with other hosting duties Thanks Igor!

Thank you to


Mark Fuhrman

@MrSaturn17


and


@wundersim


for helping us organize this contest in past editions.
Without them we could not have done this!

IMPORTANT DATES

 Earliest Date for Games to be Publicly Available: October 01, 2023 - Any game that had publicly available components online on BGG or other websites prior to the contest start date is not eligible for this contest.
 Submissions: October 01, 2023 to January 01, 2024- No further entries will be accepted after January 01, but existing entries may be further developed. By this date, entries must be playable, with components and rules available for download, though these need not necessarily be the final versions. Any game still in Idea Phase will be removed from the entry list on January 01.
 Designer Feedback Deadline: February 12, 2024 – For every entry a designer has submitted (maximum of two entries), they are required to have given (meaningful) feedback to at least 3 other games by this date (1 entry = feedback to at least 3 games, 2 entries = feedback to at least 6 games).
 Development Deadline: February 26, 2024 - Games must be complete and final (Contest Ready) by the development deadline. Any game that is not Contest Ready will be removed from the entry list.
 Typo Corrections Deadline: March 7, 2024 - Games have a 10 day period after the development deadline to make corrections in case of typos or minor component errors. After this date and until the close of voting (see below), PnP files must not be changed, so that voters all have exactly the same version of the game to evaluate. Players may still post feedback and suggestions, but these cannot be implemented until after voting closes.
 Voting Page Available: March 17, 2024 - A voting form will be made available at this time.
 Voting Deadline: March 31, 2024, and results will be announced and prizes distributed shortly afterward.

All dates are considered until 11:59:59 PM BGG Time (MT) and are based on BGG timestamps.

CONTEST PARTICIPATIONboo

This contest aims to inspire people to create innovative and fun designs, as well as further develop the talents and abilities of the designers themselves.
And for that, we invite YOU to participate! Whoever you are, and whatever skills you may have.

Whether that is reading the rules for an entry, playtesting, providing feedback and/or voting at the end, it doesn't matter! Everything is appreciated here!
Designers LOVE feedback, so please don’t hold back. However, if you don't feel like posting feedback publicly in an entry’s WIP thread, you can always send the designer a private message instead.

For designers submitting an entry, your only requirement is that you playtest and provide feedback on at least 3 other entries. If you do not comply with this requirement, your entry(s) may be declared ineligible. This will NOT, however, disqualify you from voting - everyone is encouraged to vote whether or not they have provided feedback!

Note: If entering multiple designs into the contest, you are required to provide feedback for 3 other games per game you enter.
We do this to ensure the most pleasant and fair experience for everyone in the contest, so please respect these terms or your entry will have to be disqualified, and we genuinely don't want to do that.

ENTRY REQUIREMENTS

Please check these requirements carefully to ensure that your entry is valid.

 The game should be purpose-designed for in-hand play. On-table variants are not allowed, and games will be judged on how fun they are when played in-hand.
Digital adaptations of games are allowed, however you are expected to play games physically as much as possible.

 There are NO RESTRICTIONS on theme, game length, card count or art. However, entries that are easy to build and play will probably attract more playtesters and voters.

 The game must not have had components publicly available in a WIP, as "print and play" components, or published in any form before the Earliest Date for Games to be Publicly Available, as specified above. Games that were discussed elsewhere (but without the components being available), or that were distributed privately (for private alpha playtesting) before the Earliest Date are still eligible to be entered in this contest.

 The game must not be or have been entered in any other contest here on BGG, or in any other off-site contest. Games that were entered in other contests but not completed (i.e. Withdrawn or Incomplete Entries, without components available) are still eligible to be entered in this contest.

 The game must not have had a game page on BoardGameGeek, or any other game database, before the contest. After entering the contest, games are allowed to be added.

 Second edition games are allowed. A game that is significantly different from its previous versions can enter the contest, provided you're the author of both. To enter, a new WIP post must be made for the new version, and include in the top post(s) a disclaimer that the game is a second edition, and listing how the game is different from the previous version. Second edition games can participate in all the categories.

 Entries must have a WIP thread added to the geeklist (see below), and must be Components Available before the Submission Deadline and Contest Ready before the Development Deadline.

 For the benefit of all, entrants are required to play and post feedback on at least three other games for each one that they enter. If you enter two games, give feedback on six others.

 You may create a digital version of your game on TableTop Simulator, Tabletopia, PlayingCards.io or any online platform to facilitate playtesting, and link them in your WIP thread. However, every game must also provide PnP files and a rules document, and keep them current. Games should be judged and voted on the PnP version.
Games designed to be played with a traditional deck of cards do not have to provide PnP files for their game. A rulebook is still required.

 The organizers reserve the right to make the final decision on any issues arising from the rules.

 Apps, websites or other digital aids that are used during gameplay are not allowed for this contest.
We believe that this will push designers to come up with more innovative and creative designs that do not require you to have and use a phone or similar.

SUBMITTING AN ENTRY

To submit your game to the contest, please complete each of the following steps.

 Create a "work in progress" (WIP) thread in the Works in Progress forum. If you post your WIP in a different forum, this will not disqualify your submission, but you will receive more traffic and feedback if you post to the proper forum.

 In the top post of your WIP thread, please include the following information:
* game title
* game logo
* designer/artist/graphic designer credits
* a link back to this thread (enter "[Xthread=3162927][/thread]" and remove the X)
* a short paragraph describing your game
* an image or photo of your game
* a link to the latest version of the PnP files and rules once they become available.

 Post a link to your WIP thread by replying to this post. This will help subscribers find out about your game.

 As your game develops, please discuss it within its WIP thread, not here or in the entry geeklist. To give feedback on a game, also do it in its WIP thread.

OTHER IMPORTANT DETAILS:

 You are welcome to post major announcements about your game to this thread, but please be circumspect.
When PnP files become available for your game, post the file link(s) in the top post of your WIP thread and also here. This will alert potential players that they can start to playtest your game.
Remember to update your entry in the geeklist with the latest status!

 If you need to withdraw your game, for whatever reason, simply leave a note about it here.
We're sorry to see you go, but understand that life happens!

 Entrants are required to playtest and give meaningful feedback on at least three other games for each entry of their own.
The more feedback you give others, the more you will probably receive for your own game.

 To vote, you should also aim to play as many games as you can, and you're encouraged to give meaningful feedback if you have any!


Design Categories
 Best Overall Solitaire Game - Award for the best overall solitaire game.
 Best Overall Multiplayer Game - Award for the best overall multiplayer game.
 Best Rule Book - Best written rules. Also includes rule clarity, layout, and organization.
 Most visually appealing – Best looking game. Disregarding the practicality of it (see next category).
 Clearest graphic design and support for the Visually Impaired – Most practical visual design.


Thematic/Mechanic Categories
 Best Use of Theme - Games that have an immersive theme, with gameplay mechanics that flow from the theme.
 Most Innovative Mechanic - Game with the most original mechanic or combination of mechanics.
 Best Traditional Card, Tarot, or Decktet Game - Best game designed to be played primarily with an existing deck.
 Ease of Holding – Best game designed to be comfortably held in-hand.
 Best Low Ink Printing - Games that look nice and are playable when printed in a minimal amount of ink.

NEW
 Best Playtester – For the most helpful playtesters of this contest.


Prizes and Prize Bag
 prizes may be donated to each prize category by tipping the relevant post below. Tip this main post to contribute to the Best Overall Solitaire Game and Best Overall Multiplayer Game prize. The contest fund of about 1500 that was raised will contribute 80-95 for each category and 260-280 for Best Overall Solitaire Game and Best Overall Multiplayer Game each.
Part of the fund will be used for side events and playtester spot prizes (see below). If we have a leftover, it will be split 10x for the Best Overall Solitaire Game and Best Overall Multiplayer Game prize, and 1x into every other category.

Each category will have three winners who will share the  prize pot in the ratio 4:2:1 for 1st, 2nd and 3rd place respectively.

SIDE EVENTS
Throughout the contest there will be side events hosted to promote specific playtesting and feedback, like “show us your builds” or “spot playtesting”.

The granted pot will be split or awarded by the side event’s host as they see fit at the end of the event.

Playtester Spot Prizes
The aim of this contest is to produce as many great games as possible, and to do that we don't just need games, we also need playtesters! So, to encourage playtesting there will be a system of spot prizes...

- At various times, the contest organizer will declare one or more component-available games to be eligible for playtester spot prizes and add it to this list.

- A week later a prize tip will be given to the playtester(s) who gave useful feedback in the chosen games' WIP thread during that week.

- Spot prizes will start at 10 , plus any donations tipped to the post where the target games are announced. And of course designers or anyone can also tip any playtesters that they think have been doing a good job.

- Spot prizes may run until the start of voting.

The idea is that playtesting should be ongoing, and the spot prizes will enable us to focus attention on some games that for whatever reason aren't attracting as much feedback as others.

VOTING

Everyone is encouraged to vote! It doesn’t matter to which level you have been involved in this contest. You can even vote if you have only read the rules of a game or had a look at the components, but not played the game. Whether you’ve just read the rules for a game or two, or playtested some games, you have a voice. You also don’t have to be a designer to be able to vote. The only requirement to vote is that you must have a BGG account.

In order to accommodate all voters regardless of participation level, we have decided to utilize a rating system to capture the votes.
Voters will rate games they have interacted with (in any way) on a scale of 1-10.
This system ensures fairness between voters, provides more accurate data, is generally easier to calculate, and is better at handling participants who only played a small number of the entries than other types of voting.
Because the specific “In-Hand” nature of this contest means playing the physical version of a game is highly desirable (and encouraged), for certain contest categories the voting system will take into account the degree to which a voter interacted with that entry.
Voting will be handled using google forms. You will be asked to provide your BGG username. After this, for every game, you will be asked to rate it in every category according to that category’s description. Finally, there will be an opportunity to vote for best playtester and to provide general feedback on the contest and how it was organized in the second form, if you would like to provide any.
Here are the sample forms for those who would like to take a peek ahead of time.
2023 In-Hand Game Design Contest Voting Form: Game Entries
2023 In-Hand Game Design Contest Voting Form: Best Playtester and Contest Feedback

Voters will be required to include their BGG username when they vote, to help prevent accidental or intentional multi-votes and to award playtester microbadges. However, your votes will be kept secret and will not be linked back to your username.
You do not need a Google account in order to vote.

IF YOU’RE NEW TO CONTESTS

First time entrants may find it useful to view the Design Contest FAQ for New Users helpfully provided by Chris Hansen. Please ignore anything that has to do with GDCR, since we don't have that platform anymore.

COPYRIGHT

At all times all the rights to your game stay with you. Rest assured that this is a very friendly and creative community and nobody is going to steal your ideas.
The only requirement is (obviously) that anyone should be able to legally print and assemble their own copies for personal use, for free, for the duration of the contest.

Please make sure that you have rights to all artwork, icons, etc. used in your game. There are a range of web sites to source images and icons that are free to use; there is no need to violate anyone else's copyrights. When using Creative Commons artwork, please credit the original artist(s) in your rules.






These contests are a great way to interact with fellow designers, playtest their games and in turn let people play your game. Accept both positive and negative feedback graciously, and give useful feedback in turn. You are not just participating in the contest, you are participating in the community.

Try to give more than you get. We all have different strengths and can help others more than you think (if only by playing their games and giving feedback).

Now go create some awesome games! 

License for Contest Rules
The contest rules are released under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International License. You are free to use and modify the rules for your own noncommercial contests or other projects. Please credit Chris Hansen as the original author when using these rules. This license applies only to the contest rules. It does not extend to the games entered or to the individual posts made on the contest thread.
This version of the rules was heavily based on Ben Morayta’s Solitaire PnP contest rules, which in turn were heavily based on John Kean’s 2-player contest rules.

 [IMG:bag]  prizes may be donated to each prize category by tipping the relevant post below. Tip this main post to contribute to the Best Overall Solitaire Game and Best Overall Multiplayer Game prize. The contest fund of about 1500 that was raised will contribute 80-95 [IMG:]  for each category and 260-280 [IMG:]  for Best Overall Solitaire Game and Best Overall Multiplayer Game each.
Part of the fund will be used for side events and playtester spot prizes (see below). If we have a leftover, it will be split 10x for the Best Overall Solitaire Game and Best Overall Multiplayer Game prize, and 1x into every other category.

Each category will have three winners who will share the  [IMG:bag]  prize pot in the ratio 4:2:1 for 1st, 2nd and 3rd place respectively.

SIDE EVENTS
Throughout the contest there will be side events hosted to promote specific playtesting and feedback, like “show us your builds” or “spot playtesting”.

The granted pot will be split or awarded by the side event’s host as they see fit at the end of the event.

Playtester Spot Prizes
The aim of this contest is to produce as many great games as possible, and to do that we don't just need games, we also need playtesters! So, to encourage playtesting there will be a system of spot prizes...

- At various times, the contest organizer will declare one or more component-available games to be eligible for playtester spot prizes and add it to this list.

- A week later a prize tip will be given to the playtester(s) who gave useful feedback in the chosen games' WIP thread during that week.

- Spot prizes will start at 10  [IMG:] , plus any donations tipped to the post where the target games are announced. And of course designers or anyone can also tip any playtesters that they think have been doing a good job.

- Spot prizes may run until the start of voting.

The idea is that playtesting should be ongoing, and the spot prizes will enable us to focus attention on some games that for whatever reason aren't attracting as much feedback as others.

VOTING

Everyone is encouraged to vote! It doesn’t matter to which level you have been involved in this contest. You can even vote if you have only read the rules of a game or had a look at the components, but not played the game. Whether you’ve just read the rules for a game or two, or playtested some games, you have a voice. You also don’t have to be a designer to be able to vote. The only requirement to vote is that you must have a BGG account.

In order to accommodate all voters regardless of participation level, we have decided to utilize a rating system to capture the votes.
Voters will rate games they have interacted with (in any way) on a scale of 1-10.
This system ensures fairness between voters, provides more accurate data, is generally easier to calculate, and is better at handling participants who only played a small number of the entries than other types of voting.
Because the specific “In-Hand” nature of this contest means playing the physical version of a game is highly desirable (and encouraged), for certain contest categories the voting system will take into account the degree to which a voter interacted with that entry.
Voting will be handled using google forms. You will be asked to provide your BGG username. After this, for every game, you will be asked to rate it in every category according to that category’s description. Finally, there will be an opportunity to vote for best playtester and to provide general feedback on the contest and how it was organized in the second form, if you would like to provide any.
Here are the sample forms for those who would like to take a peek ahead of time.
2023 In-Hand Game Design Contest Voting Form: Game Entries
2023 In-Hand Game Design Contest Voting Form: Best Playtester and Contest Feedback

Voters will be required to include their BGG username when they vote, to help prevent accidental or intentional multi-votes and to award playtester microbadges. However, your votes will be kept secret and will not be linked back to your username.
You do not need a Google account in order to vote.

IF YOU’RE NEW TO CONTESTS

First time entrants may find it useful to view the Design Contest FAQ for New Users helpfully provided by Chris Hansen. Please ignore anything that has to do with GDCR, since we don't have that platform anymore.

COPYRIGHT

At all times all the rights to your game stay with you. Rest assured that this is a very friendly and creative community and nobody is going to steal your ideas.
The only requirement is (obviously) that anyone should be able to legally print and assemble their own copies for personal use, for free, for the duration of the contest.

Please make sure that you have rights to all artwork, icons, etc. used in your game. There are a range of web sites to source images and icons that are free to use; there is no need to violate anyone else's copyrights. When using Creative Commons artwork, please credit the original artist(s) in your rules.



 [IMG:In-Hand Contest Bottom Banner] 

These contests are a great way to interact with fellow designers, playtest their games and in turn let people play your game. Accept both positive and negative feedback graciously, and give useful feedback in turn. You are not just participating in the contest, you are participating in the community.

Try to give more than you get. We all have different strengths and can help others more than you think (if only by playing their games and giving feedback).

Now go create some awesome games!  [IMG:thumbsup]
